tools.name: doorman_docs
tools.description: Read how Doorman works and how to integrate it (the same text as /llms.txt). Call this first if you haven't used Doorman before.

tools.name: doorman_signup
tools.description: Create a Doorman account for the user with a first form and an API key. Ask the user for their email first. They'll get an email to set a dashboard password. Creates the account's first form too and returns its id and action URL, plus the api_key (store it as DOORMAN_KEY in the project's local secre

tools.name: doorman_whoami
tools.description: Account, plan and this month's usage.

tools.name: doorman_list_forms
tools.description: List the account's forms with their action URLs and settings.

tools.name: doorman_create_form
tools.description: Create another form endpoint (one per distinct form on the site: contact, demo request, checkout, comments).

tools.name: doorman_update_form
tools.description: Change a form's settings: context, destinations, thresholds, watch mode, allow/block lists.

tools.name: doorman_get_install_snippet
tools.description: Get ready-to-paste integration code for a form on a given platform. Use 'html' for static sites, 'react' for SPA client components, and 'fetch' (plain fetch with timeout and fallback: Workers, Node, Next, Deno), 'nextjs', 'express', 'python', 'ruby' or 'elixir' when the form already posts to the pro

tools.name: doorman_test_submission
tools.description: Judge a sample message against a form's settings. Free, not forwarded, not counted. Use it to show the user Doorman working after setup (try one genuine enquiry and one sales pitch).

tools.name: doorman_send_test_delivery
tools.description: Send a sample delivery to the form's email/Slack/webhook destinations and report whether each one worked.

tools.name: doorman_list_submissions
tools.description: Recent submissions with their verdicts. Use review=true for held ones waiting for a human.

tools.name: doorman_label_submission
tools.description: Mark a submission real (delivers it if it was held or dropped) or spam.

tools.name: doorman_contact_support
tools.description: Stuck, or something isn't working? Send the problem straight to Doorman's founder, with the error you hit. Your account context (plan, forms, recent errors, never keys) is attached, and the reply goes to the account email. Use it instead of guessing at a fix.

findings.detail: Description of "doorman_signup" references sensitive artifacts (password, secret, api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: doorman_signup, doorman_list_forms, doorman_get_install_snippet, doorman_list_submissions · Private data: doorman_signup, doorman_create_form, doorman_contact_support · Public sink: doorman_signup, doorman_send_test_delivery, doorman_contact_support.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: doorman_signup, doorman_list_forms, doorman_get_install_snippet, doorman_list_submissions · Private data: doorman_signup, doorman_create_form, doorman_contact_support · Public sink: doorman_signup, doorman_send_test_delivery, doorman_contact_support

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

labels.name: doorman_label_submission

labels.name: doorman_audit_rows
labels.description: Audit old submissions: the user has a CSV export of past form submissions (Webflow, Framer, HubSpot, Formspree, Netlify, Typeform or any tool). labels.name: doorman_hubspot_map_forms
labels.description: Choose which HubSpot forms Doorman screens on a connected HubSpot account. Replaces the current list. form_id "new" makes a lead form named like the HubSpot form. Each submission's verdict is then written onto the HubSpot contact as doorman_verdict (Real, Held, Kept out).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "doorman_whoami" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Account, plan and this month's usage." → after: "Account, plan and this month's usage (checks used, and blocked_free: bots caught without reading, which don't count), and whether the account has accepted the data processing addendum (dpa)."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
